Chief_Complaint.content: 3-day history of watery diarrhea occurring approximately 6–7 times per day
Diarrhea requires staying near toilet and impacts activities of daily living and work
Chief_Complaint.source_text: needs to stay near toilet; impacts ADLs/work

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Watery diarrhea for 3 days occurring approximately 6–7 times per day
Left lower quadrant crampy intermittent abdominal pain without radiation to the back
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: LLQ crampy intermittent abd pain; no radiation to back

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports feeling weak and shaky
Patient reports no blood in stool
Vomiting occurred at onset of illness and has now resolved
Felt hot and feverish at onset 3–4 days ago with no current fever and temperature not measured
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Felt hot/feverish at onset 3–4 days ago; no current fever; temp not measured

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Decreased appetite but tolerating fluids and eating soups and smoothies
Possible trigger identified as Chinese restaurant takeaway eaten 4 days ago with friends
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Possible trigger: Chinese restaurant takeaway 4 days ago; ate out with friends

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Exposure history includes one child who vomited but had no diarrhea and no others with similar symptoms
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Exposures: one child vomited; no diarrhea; no others with similar sx

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports no prior gastrointestinal or bowel problems
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: GI hx: Denies prior tummy/bowel problems

Past_Medical_History.content: History of asthma that is well controlled

Medications.content: Plan to use oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte from pharmacy
Medications.source_text: Oral hydration; ORS (e.g., Dioralyte) from pharmacy

Medications.content: Paracetamol 2 tablets up to 4 times per day for fever and aches for the first few days
Medications.source_text: Paracetamol 2 tabs up to 4x/day for fever/aches first few days

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is attending work but finding it difficult due to symptoms
Patient lives with wife and two children

Assessment.content: Acute gastroenteritis characterized by 3 days of watery diarrhea, left lower quadrant crampy pain, initial vomiting and subjective fever, no blood in stool, maintaining oral intake, and possibly food-borne after takeaway, likely viral per discussion
Assessment.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis—3 days watery diarrhea, LLQ crampy pain, initial vomiting and subjective fever; no blood; maintaining PO; possible food-borne after takeaway (likely viral per discussion)

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise oral hydration and use of oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte from pharmacy for acute gastroenteritis
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Oral hydration; ORS (e.g., Dioralyte) from pharmacy

Plan_of_Care.content: Paracetamol 2 tablets up to 4 times daily for fever and aches in the first few days for acute gastroenteritis
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Paracetamol 2 tabs up to 4x/day for fever/aches first few days

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommend rest and taking 2–3 days off work for acute gastroenteritis
If acute gastroenteritis not improved in 3–4 days, patient to return for consideration of stool sample and further tests
Plan_of_Care.source_text: If not improved in 3–4 days, return; consider stool sample and further tests

Follow_up_Information.content: If not improved in 3–4 days, patient should return for reassessment and possible stool sample and further tests
Follow_up_Information.source_text: If not improved in 3–4 days, return; consider stool sample and further tests
